fields.v: - Gated SDD workflow + Claude Code + Claude Opus 5 (claude-opus-5; 21 of 4,483 responses on Claude Opus 5.5): no success criterion stated by the authors (they report what the controls recorded; no ground truth, no control condition). 5 of 9 features completed with all tasks done; 288/581 tasks done. Executor left 1 undeclared durable change in resources/ (caught); orchestrator flagged 11/247 checks (6 cloud-sync client, 3 in-round author requests, 1 verification build products, 1 executor syntax-check caches) and stopped in 4; tried to rewrite a stop as pass; absorbed changes into new baselines; dispatched unapproved tasks. Reviewer: blocking in first review of 15/20 artefacts; 11.74M tokens. Quality verdict: no criterion stated by the authors. Cost verdict: no criterion stated by the authors (unrequested re-reviews took 75.3% of reviewer tokens in P1, P2, P5)
fields.quote: These results describe what the checks recorded, not what the controls prevented. Since there is no condition in which the scope declaration or the check is absent, the scarcity of out-of-scope edits by the executor cannot be credited to either of them.
fields.where: §5.2 RQ1: block checks and the stop rule, p. 9
fields.why: The authors state no success criterion for quality or cost (descriptive audit-trail study without ground truth or control), so the 'partly' quality and cost verdicts are the extractor's judgement, which the 2026-11-23 rule replaces with 'no criterion stated by the authors'.
fields.doubt: O artigo é descritivo e os autores não definem critério de sucesso (nem de qualidade nem de custo); dizem que os resultados descrevem o que os controlos registaram, não o que preveniram (pág. 9). Os veredictos 'partly' são juízo teu. Pela regra de 23-11, troca ambos por 'no criterion stated by the authors' e mantém os números.
